Health Insurance. All regular full-time employees have the option to enroll in the City's Health Insurance Plan. These plans are described on separate documents provided by the insurance carrier and are available from the City Clerk.
COBRA. The Federal Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) gives employees and their qualified beneficiaries the opportunity to continue health insurance coverage under the City's health plan when a "qualifying event" would normally result in the loss of eligibility. Length of continued coverage will be determined by COBRA regulations. Under COBRA, the employee or beneficiary pays the full cost of the coverage at the City's group rates, and, at the City's discretion, up to a 2% administrative fee.

If an employee should suffer a work-related injury or disease, as provided by law he/she will receive benefits through the City's Workers' Compensation Policy, which is paid for entirely by the City. Employees may use sick leave until Workers' Compensation benefits become effective. Once benefits become effective the employee may use sick leave to supplement workers' compensation pay up to 100% of employee's regular pay. This program provides for payment of medical expenses and weekly compensation payments, as allowed by law. Workers' Compensation leave will run concurrent with FMLA leave.
Life Insurance. Each regular full-time employee is provided life insurance at no cost to the employee.
Other Benefits.
Social Security and/or other benefits will be available to employees in connection with his/her employment with the City, once they complete their probationary period.
Employees who elect dependent coverage with any benefit plan offered by the City must carry their dependents in accordance with all governing laws and plan agreements. Changes in dependent status must be reported to the City Clerk within 31 days of the event. Violation of any benefits, governing laws, plan agreements, or City policies relating to benefits may lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination.
Retirement. The City adopted a retirement plan for all regular full-time employees. A copy of the Master Plan, all revisions, and details of the plan are available in the City Clerk's office.

1. Purpose. The purpose of this section is to inform all employees of many of the types of conduct that may result in adverse personnel action, and to prescribe guidelines that should be utilized by management when disciplinary actions are needed due to violations of work rules or failure to meet standards of performance or conduct. The City generally adheres to the concept of "progressive discipline." However, the City is neither obligated nor required to follow this concept at any time including a first offense.
2. Types of Disciplinary Action. The following types of disciplinary action may be taken against any City employee covered by this Policy:
a. Oral Warning. Any employee may be called in at any time for a private conference with his or her supervisor regarding unacceptable behavioral patterns or work performance. The conference shall be documented in the employee's personnel file by his or her supervisor as soon as possible. Documentation shall include the nature of the offense, the reprimand, improvements to be made, and any relevant discussions pertaining to the matter. An employee receiving an oral warning does not have appeal rights.
b. Notice of Concern. A notice of concern may be given to an employee when an oral warning has not resulted in the desired improvement or if the incident requires greater discipline than an oral warning. A copy of the notice shall be placed in the personnel file of the employee as soon as possible. An employee receiving a notice of concern does not have appeal rights. Documentation shall include the nature of the offense, the reprimand, improvements to be made, and any relevant discussions pertaining to the matter.
c. Suspension with or without Pay. An employee may be suspended with or without pay for failure to report to assigned duties, negligence, delinquency, or inefficiency in performing duties, misconduct, insubordination, or for other reasons, including but not limited to those reasons listed in subsection 3 of this section of the Personnel Policy Handbook as well as any additional reasons for disciplinary action listed within the handbook. Said suspension may be:
1. For a prescribed period of time, not to exceed 30 days as a disciplinary measure for a serious violation or for repeated offenses; or
2. For an indefinite period of time pending the outcome of an inquiry or investigation of charges.
An employee suspended for a prescribed length of time as a disciplinary measure shall not be allowed to use vacation, sick, or any other leave during the period of suspension.
d. Disciplinary Salary Reduction. An employee's salary may be reduced from one pay step to a lower step for disciplinary purposes. The salary reduction does not constitute a demotion in pay grade.
e. Disciplinary Demotion. An employee may be demoted due to unfitness to perform assigned duties; negligence, delinquency, or inefficiency in performing duties; misconduct; insubordination; or for other reasons not stated above. Effective September 13, 2011, a disciplinary demotion shall be accompanied by a salary reduction consistent with the City's Compensation Plan. Exceptions may be made with the approval of the City Manager.
g. Dismissal. An employee may be dismissed due to delinquency, misconduct, inefficiency, inability to perform assigned work in a satisfactory manner, or for other reasons not stated above. Prior to an employee being dismissed, the Department Head shall first obtain concurrence from the City Manager. Notice of dismissal to employee shall be dated and in writing and placed in the employee's personnel file.
An employee may be placed on probation as a result of a disciplinary action for a period of time during which the Supervisor or Department Head will determine if the employee's performance meets the expectations of that Department.
3. Cause for Disciplinary Action.
Realizing the inability to categorize all fact situations that may arise in the employment relationship, this listing is only illustrative of the types of behavior that may warrant discipline and is neither complete nor exclusive. It serves only as a guideline. Actual discipline shall be determined with due consideration for the facts and circumstances surrounding each case. The severity of discipline will be appropriate to the offense, with the Department Head taking into account all mitigating or extenuating circumstances including, but not limited to, whether the offense was willful or a result of lack of knowledge or information, the overall work record of the employee, and how many and how frequent previous offenses have been, etc.
The violation of any of these rules will result in disciplinary action ranging from an oral warning to dismissal:
A. Habitual tardiness or absenteeism.
B. Failure to report immediately to the supervisor any job-related accident or injury or unsafe working condition.
C. Excessive disciplinary actions within a one-year period.
D. Failure to report an off-the-job accident or injury that may affect the performance of your job.
E. Failure to report harassment of any kind.
F. Use of tobacco products on City property.
G. Gambling during work or on City property.
H. Working on personal business or projects on City time.
I. Creating or contributing to unsanitary or disorderly housekeeping conditions.
J. Failing to notify the City promptly when you will be absent from work or late to work.
K. Soliciting employees while either the person being solicited or the person doing the soliciting is on work time. This applies to selling of any type; solicitation of memberships, pledges, or subscriptions; circulating petitions; or collecting money. Employees may be permitted, with prior approval of the City Manager, passive solicitation for non-profit purposes.
L. Conduct that endangers you or another employee.
M. Unauthorized use of City tools, equipment, telephones or other City property.
N. Failure to use safety equipment required by the City or to comply with safety rules.
O. Distribution of literature or printed material of any kind in the work area or during work time or posting or removing notices, signs or other written materials.
P. Remaining on or coming onto City work premises during off-duty hours for purposes other than to work without advance approval. (Employees may report early and/or leave late due to transportation arrangements.)
Q. Sleeping, loafing on the job, engaging in horseplay, throwing anything that may harm another, playing jokes or otherwise distracting or startling others, acting in a disorderly manner or being away from your work station unnecessarily.
R. Refusal or failure to carry out instructions or to perform work assignments as required by supervisory personnel.
S. Negligence, carelessness, or abuse resulting in the damage, destruction, or misplacement of tools, machinery, equipment, products, materials, or other property belonging to the City or to others.
T. Removing City property from work site without written authorization.
U. Operating or tampering with City equipment that had not been authorized to use or repair.
V. Restricting work production, encouraging or persuading others to restrict work production or supporting an interruption of work.
W. Inefficiency or ineffectiveness on the job.
X. Obtaining materials or tools on fraudulent orders or misrepresentations.
Y. Bringing and/or consuming alcohol, drugs, or narcotics at work or working on the job under the influence of alcohol, drugs or narcotics.
Z. Carrying explosives or unauthorized weapons on a work site.
AA. Deliberate action causing damage or destruction or waste of tools, machinery, equipment, product, materials or other property belonging to the City, a City official or to a fellow worker.
BB. Giving false information in making application for employment, on any City document, or pursuant to any City inquiry or investigation, or giving false statements to any supervisor, official, public, or board.
CC. Immoral or indecent conduct on a work site, including abusive or threatening language to any employee and the making of false or malicious statements or defaming another employee, City Official or the City.
DD. Fighting or attempting bodily injury to others on a work site except in clear cases of self-defense.
EE. Stealing or hiding any property of other employees, persons, City Officials or the City.
FF. Failure to return to work from an authorized leave-of-absence.
GG. Divulging confidential information to an unauthorized person or making any disclosure of confidential information regarding the City to any person, agency, publication, radio or television station without authorization from the City.
HH. Abusive conduct, verbal or physical, toward a fellow employee, City official or member of the public.
II. Conduct, comments, or activity that adversely affects the morale and productivity of the department or that discredits a co-worker, superior, or the City.
JJ. Racial slurs.
KK. Sexual harassment and other forms of harassment.
LL. Loss of certification or license required to perform job duties.
MM. Inability to meet certification requirements within required time frame.
NN. If there is reasonable cause to believe that employee violated local and city ordinances, and/or Federal or State laws, administrative regulations, or departmental rules.

Employees released on bail, or on their own recognizance after being arrested or charged with a crime, may, at the discretion of the City, continue in their jobs until the outcome of their trial or court appearance is known. Absences from work due to incarceration and/or court appearances will be charged against any available vacation leave balances, or taken without pay, at the option of the employee. Employees convicted of a felony, or of a misdemeanor involving serious moral turpitude, shall be dismissed from City employment. Employees convicted in any court for offenses of a nature, which tend to cast discredit upon the City government and/or a department of the City will be considered for immediate dismissal (e.g., an employee convicted of DUI, whether incarcerated or not). 1. Right to Appeal.
Any employee covered by this policy, with the exception of probationary employees, who has been suspended, demoted, suffered a reduction in pay or dismissed as a result of a disciplinary action shall have a right to appeal the adverse action to the City Manager. Employees who have received an oral or written warning do not have appeal or grievance or name clearing hearing rights.
An appeal is a formal review of an adverse action as defined herein. The written notification of an adverse action to the employee will contain the following:
a. The effective date of the action;
b. The specific charges or reasons for the action;
c. A statement informing the employee that he or she is encouraged to initiate an informal discussion of the action in which the appeal is based or the employee may initiate a formal appeal in writing to the City Manager;
d. A warning that failure to respond within the prescribed time frame to the City Manager will result in a waiver of all further appeal rights.
Employees are encouraged to initiate an informal discussion of the adverse action with their Department Head within five (5) calendar days of receiving the adverse action. The Department Head, after meeting with employee, will respond in writing to the employee within ten (10) calendar days. Extenuating circumstances may extend response time and written notice of the extension will be given to employee. If after informal discussion with the Department Head the employee is not satisfied with the Department Head's written response employee may file a formal appeal in writing to the City Manager within five (5) calendar days of the Department Head's response.
2. Procedure. If an employee chooses to pursue an appeal of an adverse action, the appeal must include:
a. Name, address, and telephone number of the appellant.
b. A statement describing what is being appealed.
c. Names of any witnesses with first-hand knowledge of incident.
d. The supervisor or Department Head through whom the employee has attempted to resolve the appeal on an informal basis if an informal discussion was initiated.
e. The relief that the employee desires in making the appeal.
In the event the employee is not comfortable conducting an informal discussion with his/her Department Head, employee may file a formal appeal opposing the adverse action in writing within five (5) calendar days of receiving the adverse action directly to the City Manager. In the event the employee does not respond within five (5) calendar days of receiving the adverse action, the action becomes final and the employee will have waived all further appeal rights.
The City Manager, after considering the employee's response to the adverse action, will give the employee written notification of his/her findings within ten (10) calendar days. Extenuating circumstances may extend response time and written notice of the extension will be given to employee. The decision of the Manager shall be final. For direct reports to the City Manager, appeals would go directly to the Mayor and Council.
1446:
1. Purpose.
The City recognizes that differences of opinion may occur in the interpretation of specific policies and the manner in which policies are enforced. For this reason the Council has established the following procedure to address grievances.
This procedure is designed to:
a. Provide for a systematic and orderly method for resolving complaints and differences of opinion between employees and supervisory personnel.
b. Insure that all employees are afforded a fair, equitable, and expeditious review of their grievances without fear, coercion, or discrimination.
c. Set forth a procedure governing presentation of charges hearing opportunities, and appeals to the City Manager.
2. Employee Grievance Opportunity.
Any regular service employee shall have the opportunity to secure consideration of any grievance as heretofore defined.
Notwithstanding any other provision in this policy manual, any employee may file a grievance alleging a violation of the City's equal employment opportunity policy regarding any employment action he or she may believe adversely affects his or her employment. Grievance shall be filed directly with the City Manager.
3. Responsibilities of Management.
Supervisory and management personnel shall hear and consider any employee grievance without prejudice. Supervisory and management personnel shall take necessary and appropriate corrective action when warranted, and, when appropriate, they shall provide a reasonable explanation as to why the grievance is not justified.
No supervisor shall deny an employee the opportunity to take the grievance to the next step in the grievance procedure when said grievance cannot be settled to the satisfaction of the employee at the lower level. Should such a denial occur, the employee shall be entitled to file a new grievance, based on such denial, at the next level of supervision.
4. Grievance Procedure Steps.
Step One.
The employee shall present his/her grievance to the immediate supervisor in writing. A grievance request must be presented within five (5) calendar days of the date employee could reasonably be expected to have knowledge of the existence of the grievance.
Upon being informed of the grievance, the immediate supervisor shall make appropriate inquiries and take necessary actions to resolve the problem, or provide the employee with a written answer, typically within ten (10) calendar days, absent extenuating circumstances.
Step Two.
In the event the problem is not resolved, or if the employee is dissatisfied with the decision of the immediate supervisor, or a reply has not been furnished as outlined in Step One, the employee may submit the grievance in writing to the Department Head.
A written reply from the Department Head shall be furnished to the employee, typically within ten (10) calendar days, absent extenuating circumstances.
Step Three. If the employee is still aggrieved, he/she may, within ten (10) calendar days of receipt of the Department Head's response, submit the grievance in writing to the City Manager. Said request shall contain all applicable facts concerning the grievance. The City Manager shall render a decision in writing to the aggrieved, typically within ten (10) calendar days, absent extenuating circumstances. The decision of the City Manager shall be final. For situations involving the City Manager and a direct report the direct report shall submit the grievance in writing to the Mayor and Council.
5. Management Prerogatives. The following areas of personnel administration are considered management prerogatives and are not subject to grievance review unless there is evidence of abuse and discretion in the exercise of these prerogatives. The City Manager shall make this determination.
a. Scheduling and assigned work.
b. Establishing work standards and quality.
c. Size of work force and reorganizations.
d. Reductions in work force.
e. The City's Pay Classification Plan.
f. Content or rating of a performance appraisal.
g. Decisions, policies, practices, resolutions, or ordinances made or passed by the City Council.
1447:
1. Resignations. It is preferred that at least a fourteen (14) calendar day notice be given by an employee who wishes to voluntarily resign his/her position with the City. Said notice must be given in writing. Department Heads and/or those employees covered by contract are obligated to give notice as provided by contract, and if not included in the contract, a notice of at least thirty (30) days is preferred. Said notice must be given in writing. Improper notification will be taken into consideration if a request to rehire is received.
2. Abandonment of Position. Failure to report to work for three or more consecutive workdays without proper notification and authorization shall be cause for dismissal and shall be documented as abandonment of position.
3. Reduction in Work Force.
An involuntary separation not involving a delinquency, misconduct, or inefficiency shall be considered a lay-off. The City Manager may lay-off an employee in the City service and may base such a decision on the Department Head's recommendation in accordance with all Federal and State laws when he/she deems it necessary by reason of shortage of work or funds, the abolishment of the position, or other material changes in duty of organization, or for related reasons which are outside the employee's control and which do not reflect discredit upon the service of the employee. The duties performed by the laid-off employee may be reassigned to other employees already working who hold a position in an appropriate class. No classified service employee shall be separated while there are temporary or probationary employees serving the same function in the department, unless the classified service employee is not willing to transfer to the position held by the temporary or probationary employee.
When a reduction in the work force becomes necessary, consideration shall be given to the quality of each employee's past performance, organizational needs, and seniority in determining those employees to be retained.
Employees separated from service through no fault of their own may receive preference in rehiring should a position for which they are qualified open, excluding employees with prior unsatisfactory performance appraisal or disciplinary actions, but all hiring decisions are made at the discretion of the City.
4. Retirement. Employees may retire from the City under the City's Defined Benefit Retirement Plan as adopted by the Mayor and Council. A copy of the Master Plan is held in the office of the City Clerk.
5. Separation through Death. Separation shall be effective as of the date of death of any employee covered by this policy. All compensation due including payment for time worked and payment for any accrued annual leave shall be paid to the designated beneficiary or beneficiaries or estate of the employee except for such sums which by law must be paid to the surviving spouse.
6. Dismissal. An employee may be dismissed from employment as outlined in Section XIII 2 (f). Written notice of dismissal to employee shall be dated and in writing and placed in the employee's personnel file.
